post_understanding.summary: A MySQL application query against an issues/projects schema is very slow (~15 seconds). The query filters on issues.subject with a leading-wildcard LIKE, joins to projects, and uses correlated subqueries on enabled_modules and members for permissions, returning 10 rows ordered by issues.id DESC.
symptoms: high rows examined (EXPLAIN shows ~311k rows on issues)
application perceived as slow under up to ~100 concurrent users
suspected_root_causes: leading-wildcard LIKE on issues.subject prevents index use causing large scan
use of LOWER() on subject further prevents index use (unless CI collation makes it redundant)
correlated/DEPENDENT subqueries (EXISTS on enabled_modules, IN subquery on members) per-project overhead
ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10 causing scan to find matches before it can limit
key_evidence: EXPLAIN rows for issues: 311632 with key PRIMARY and Using where
Dependent subqueries appear in EXPLAIN (DEPENDENT SUBQUERY on members and enabled_modules)
Tables sizes: issues ~334,823 rows; projects 494; concurrent users up to 100
assumptions: MySQL/InnoDB is used (based on schema and EXPLAIN), version 5.6/5.7 without functional indexes; no fulltext index on issues.subject
Database collation is case-insensitive (e.g., utf8_general_ci), making LOWER() redundant but not aiding index use with a leading wildcard
Issues.id is the PRIMARY KEY; there is a secondary index on issues.project_id; no index on LOWER(subject) or generated column for subject
Members has an index on user_id (as hinted by index_members_on_user_id in EXPLAIN); enabled_modules has an index on project_id
Data distribution: only a very small fraction of issues.subject contains the substring '255392' (or similar search tokens), forcing most of the table to be scanned
The IN lists of project IDs in the query correspond to existing projects IDs in the dataset
Hardware and buffer pool sizes are modest so that scanning ~300k+ rows results in multi-second latency; cold cache effects are acceptable for reproduction
Semijoin optimizations are not transforming subqueries into joins (as EXPLAIN shows DEPENDENT SUBQUERY); if needed, optimizer_switch may be adjusted at session level in the experiment

generated_data_plan.rationale: Ensure a large scan due to leading-wildcard LIKE and meaningful distribution for permission filters.

anomaly_injection.name: Slow subject search with leading wildcard
anomaly_injection.method: Execute the provided query containing LOWER(subject) LIKE '%255392%' which prevents index usage due to leading wildcard; ensure no fulltext/functional index exists on subject and collation is case-insensitive.

parameters.query_text: SELECT issues.* FROM `issues` INNER JOIN `projects` ON `projects`.`id` = `issues`.`project_id` WHERE (((`projects`.`status` <> 9 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 AS one FROM enabled_modules em WHERE em.project_id = projects.id AND em.name = 'issue_tracking')) AND (((`projects`.`is_public` = 1 AND `projects`.`id` NOT IN (SELECT project_id FROM members WHERE user_id IN (44, 638)) AND ((`issues`.`is_private` = 0 OR `issues`.`author_id` = 44 OR `issues`.`assigned_to_id` IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (`projects`.`id` IN (1, 6, 9, 13, 115, 129, 131, 136, 186, 227, 228, 230, 275, 287, 315, 335, 340, 369, 394, 404, 408, 450, 453, 454, 456, 458, 460, 462, 492, 511, 512, 516, 519, 527, 531, 533, 537) AND ((`issues`.`is_private` = 0 OR `issues`.`author_id` = 44 OR `issues`.`assigned_to_id` IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (`projects`.`id` IN (40, 68, 130, 149, 326, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 402, 455, 514, 515, 528) AND (1 = 1)) OR (`projects`.`id` IN (91, 111, 128, 130, 149, 235, 257, 322, 326, 328, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 489, 508, 514, 515, 525, 528) AND ((`issues`.`is_private` = 0 OR `issues`.`author_id` = 44 OR `issues`.`assigned_to_id` IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (`projects`.`id` IN (457) AND ((`issues`.`is_private` = 0 OR `issues`.`author_id` = 44 OR `issues`.`assigned_to_id` IN (44, 186, 898))))))) AND (`issues`.`id` != 251880) AND (LOWER(`issues`.`subject`) LIKE LOWER('%255392%'))) ORDER BY `issues`.`id` DESC LIMIT 10;
parameters.optimizer_switch: semijoin=off (if version >= 5.7 and needed to reproduce DEPENDENT SUBQUERY)

query_or_transaction_effects: The slow query returns up to 10 issues ordered by id DESC after scanning most of the issues table.
Dependent subqueries (EXISTS/IN) are evaluated per candidate project, contributing additional overhead.
Under concurrency, overall throughput drops and individual latencies increase.
validation_criteria: Reproduced EXPLAIN plan shows issues using PRIMARY (or no subject index) with Using where and high rows estimate.
Measured rows_examined per execution is near the issues row count.
Single-thread execution time of the provided query is >= 10s on the generated dataset.
Under the 100-thread surge, average and p95 latencies increase further and server shows elevated IO/CPU.
